1.why: Every MFA endpoint derives the account exclusively from the authenticated session via recordFor(session.accountId), with no client-supplied account identifier accepted anywhere.

2.why: Identity codes are generated per pre-auth session and checked only against that session's own stored identityCode, so a code issued for one account cannot verify another.

3.why: The /api/mfa/confirm handler does not delete or rotate any existing sessions, so all prior sessions in the sessions map keep working until idle/absolute timeout or explicit logout.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted (encryptSecret) and recovery codes are stored as peppered HMAC-SHA-256 hashes (recoveryHash), never in plain text.

5.why: All tokens, identity codes, TOTP secrets, recovery codes, keys, and IVs are generated with crypto.getRandomValues or crypto.subtle.generateKey, which are cryptographically secure.

6.why: Session and pre-auth tokens exist only in HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Strict cookies, the CSRF token and provisioning secret live only in JS memory/DOM, and no localStorage or sessionStorage is used.

7.why: The server validates and normalises all inputs with strict regexes and type checks (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, normaliseRecovery, apiBody shape check) and there are no SQL queries to inject.

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered with textContent while innerHTML is assigned only static markup, and the nonce-based CSP without unsafe-inline prevents injected script execution.

9.why: The application performs no HTTP redirects at all and the client navigates only between fixed internal views and hardcoded API paths, so no open redirect is possible.

10.why: Every response sets Content-Security-Policy (including frame-ancestors 'none'), Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY.

11.why: secureCookie applies HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict to both the __Host-session and __Host-preauth cookies.

12.why: Server-side logging is clean and errors are generic with no stack traces, but in the default TEST_MODE the identity code and recovery codes are deliberately written to the browser console and the on-page Logs panel.

13.why: Identity codes expire after 10 minutes and are marked used then deleted on success, TOTP setup counters are recorded to block replay, and recovery codes are invalidated after a single use.

14.why: Five failed attempts trigger a 10-minute lockout (MAX_FAILURES/LOCK_MS with failAttempt/locked) on identity verification, MFA confirm, and recovery endpoints.

15.why: A fresh random session token is issued at authentication with the pre-auth cookie expired, sessions enforce 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the server-side session and expires the cookie.
